resolutions.researcher_notes: No source found that says this project was formally cancelled. Multiple independent sources (MEED 2007, World Bank Regional Gas Trade report Feb 2013, Libya Herald June 2013) describe the Mellitah-Gabes ('Joint Gas') pipeline as a stalled/dormant proposal that was STILL being discussed and 'developed'/'on the agenda' as late as 2013 -- five years after the row's CancelledYear=2008. No cancellation announcement, contract termination, or formal shelving event was located in English or Arabic sources for any year. Best-supported characterization: never built, status quiet/uncertain for years at a time, but not affirmatively sourced as 'cancelled' in 2008 or any other year. Recommend Update review the value (candidate: shelved/uncertain rather than a dated cancellation) but I am not asserting a replacement value myself.
Both sources consistently describe this as a natural gas transmission pipeline (part of the 'Joint Gas' scheme moving Libyan gas to the Tunisian domestic market). Fuel=Gas is well supported.

Could not source 1996 specifically. MEED (2007) states the project 'was originally proposed in 1997' -- a one-year discrepancy from the row's ProposalYear=1996. No source found pinning 1996 exactly. Flagging the mismatch rather than certifying either year; 1997 (MEED) is the closest sourced figure if Update wants to revise.

Evidence actually CONTRADICTS 2006 as a shelving year: the World Bank report (Feb 2013, Report No. 76114-MEN) states 'In June 2006 it was announced that Joint Gas had awarded a contract for engineering consulting services to the British firm, Penspen. In August 2006, Joint Gas approved a budget of $250 million for the project' -- i.e. 2006 was a year of forward progress (contract award + budget approval), not shelving. No source describes a 2006 shelving event. Flagging this as a likely-wrong date rather than sourcing it.

No source states the project was cancelled in 2008 or any year. Contradicting evidence: Libya Herald (June 2013) reports the pipeline plan was 'on the agenda' in bilateral Libya-Tunisia ministerial energy talks in Tripoli, and the World Bank report (Feb 2013) describes Libya as able to 'follow up on the Mellitah-Gabes pipeline to Tunisia, which is being developed by a Tunisian-Libyan joint venture, Joint Gas' -- present-tense, no mention of cancellation. Both post-date the row's claimed 2008 cancellation by 5 years. See __VALIDITY__ for full discussion.

Three independent sources agree on ~2 bcm/y: MEED states 'up to 70,000 million cubic feet a year' (~1.98 bcm/y, matching 193.5 MMcf/d x 365 almost exactly); World Bank report gives '1.0 to 2.0 bcm of gas per year'; Al Bayan (2002) states the Tunisian market would receive 'about two billion cubic meters of gas' annually. Row's 193.5 MMcf/d (1.98 bcm/y) is well corroborated.

Al Bayan (2002) states the pipeline is 275 km total (205 km within Tunisia) -- an EXACT match to the row's 275 km. MEED and the World Bank report give 264-266 km (a minor, plausible variance likely reflecting different route-segment conventions or later re-surveys, e.g. Libya-side vs. total). Overall well supported; the 264-266 vs 275 spread should be noted but is not a material conflict.

World Bank report (Regional Gas Trade Projects in Arab Countries, Report No. 76114-MEN, Feb 2013) repeatedly states the pipeline is '24-inch-diameter' / '24 inches in diameter', an exact match to the row's Diameter=24 in. This is the only independent source found that states a diameter; treating as medium (1 strong) rather than high since it is not independently corroborated by a second source.

Existing FuelSource url re-verified live (200, Arabic text present: '...270 مليون دولار...'). Content directly discusses this exact project: Mellitah-Gabes, 275 km (205 km in Tunisia), $270M cost split 50/50, STEG + NOC joint venture, ~2 bcm/y -- and is independently corroborated by MEED, the World Bank report, and euro-petrole/Sofregaz on essentially every data point. Note: url_verifier required an Arabic expected-substring ('270 مليون دولار') -- a Latin-script 'Mellitah' substring check failed even though the page is live and on-topic (Arabic transliteration only).
Start=Mellitah, Libya and End=Gabes, Tunisia are consistently and repeatedly confirmed across every source found (MEED, World Bank, Al Bayan, Sofregaz/euro-petrole, Libya Herald). Not in dispute.

Al Bayan (2002) states the total project cost at 'approximately $270 million USD, to be split equally between the two countries' -- an EXACT match to the row's SegmentCost=270,000,000 USD. However, the cost figure moved over time in other sources: MEED cites an original ~$300 million estimate, and the World Bank report separately gives 'Capital cost $323.55 million' in a project table and notes 'In August 2006, Joint Gas approved a budget of $250 million.' Treating as medium tier: one exact match plus a range of other cited figures ($250-323.55M) from different points in the project's life, none of which is a clean second confirmation of $270M specifically.

Recovered the origin akhbarlibya24.net piece (2020-05-10; verified 200 OK, contains 'بوصة'). Full text (via translation) says: Mellitah Oil & Gas's Operations Dept. was building a 4-inch BACKUP gas line from the main production station to the GT11/GT12 power-generation units at Abu Attifel field, needed because those units currently depend solely on the NGL plant; as of the article the work was ~60% complete, expected done by end of May 2020. Nothing in this source says the project was cancelled -- it reads as an active, nearly-finished project. Searched further (English + Arabic: Libya Herald/Observer, attaqa, eanlibya, NOC.ly, Mellitah OG site, Oil Review Africa/Petroleum Africa Abu Attifel coverage) for any later update (completion notice, abandonment, incident) -- found none either way; Abu Attifel field itself has continued normal maintenance/restart cycles through 2020-2024 with no reported disruption tied to this specific backup line. Cannot source Status=cancelled from any independent reporting. Separately: GEM's own wiki page for this same PID (read for leads only, not cited) currently carries Status='Under construction', not cancelled -- i.e. the tracker's own reference material disagrees internally with the sheet's cancelled value, another sign 'cancelled' has no support. No ShelvedCancelledType is recorded either, consistent with the value never having been substantiated. Recommend: revert Status question to the researcher/human reviewer -- evidence points away from cancelled, not toward it.

The article's own title/text is explicitly 'خط الغاز' (gas line); it is a natural-gas backup feed line, supporting Fuel=Gas. Single strong primary source (the announcement itself); no second independent outlet covered this local project, so tier=medium, independent=false.
Dated 2020-05-10, describing the line as under active construction (~60% complete, expected finished by end of that month) -- supports ConstructionYear=2020. Single source, tier=medium.
Text explicitly states 'خط احتياطي بقطر 4 بوصة' (a backup line of 4-inch diameter) -- directly supports Diameter=4/in. Single source, tier=medium.

The recorded StartLocation/EndLocation (Mellitah Port -> Bu-Attifel oil field, ~900-1000 km apart) are NOT supported by the source and are almost certainly a mis-parse of the headline. 'مليتة' in the title is Mellitah Oil & Gas COMPANY (the operator, a joint venture of NOC/Eni), not the geographic Mellitah industrial complex/port. The article describes the line as running entirely WITHIN the Abu Attifel field: from the field's main production station to the on-site GT11/GT12 electricity-generation units, as a backup supply route for when the field's own NGL plant is down for maintenance. There is no route to or from the Mellitah coastal complex at all. See __VALIDITY__ for full discussion; recommend both Start/EndLocation be corrected to reflect a short intra-field line at Abu Attifel, not a Mellitah-to-Sirte-Basin transmission route.

resolutions.researcher_notes: (a) OWNER: GAZ-SYSTEM is not supported by any source and looks like an entity-linkage error, as flagged. FIVE independent sources -- Al Bayan (2002, Arabic), MEED (2007), euro-petrole/Sofregaz project-reference page (2004), Libya Herald (2013), and a World Bank regional gas-trade report (Feb 2013) -- consistently identify the developer/owner as a Libya-Tunisia 50:50 joint venture variously named 'Tunisian-Libyan Gas Transportation Company', 'Joint Gas', or 'Joint Gas Company', formed by Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) and Tunisia's Societe Tunisienne de l'Electricite et du Gaz (STEG; Al Bayan's Arabic gives 'الشركة التونسية للكهرباء والغاز' = STEG, and 'المؤسسة الوطنية الليبية للنفط' = NOC). No source mentions Eni, Mellitah Oil & Gas, ETAP, or Sonatrach as owner of THIS pipeline. Recommend Update replace/flag the GAZ-SYSTEM/parent attribution as unsupported and consider NOC + STEG (via the Joint Gas / Tunisian-Libyan Gas Transportation Company JV) as the sourced owner, subject to normal entity-lookup/dedup before staging. (b) EXISTENCE & CANCELLATION: The project is real and well documented as distinct from Greenstream (Mellitah-Gela, to Italy, built 2004) and from the domestic Tunisian El Borma-Gabes / South Tunisia (Nawara) lines -- multiple sources explicitly describe it as a SEPARATE Libya-to-Tunisia export line via the Joint Gas JV, 264-275 km, 24-inch, ~1-2 bcm/y, first floated 1996/1997, JV formalized ~2003, engineering (Sofregaz) completed 2004, contract to Penspen awarded June 2006, Joint Gas approved a $250M budget August 2006, MEED (Oct 2007) describes it as stalled in tendering with no EPC contract issued, and it was STILL on the bilateral agenda in June 2013 (Libya Herald) and described in present tense as 'being developed' by the World Bank as of Feb 2013. No source anywhere states an actual cancellation event, in 2008 or any year -- the 2013 evidence directly contradicts a 2008 cancellation (project was still under active government discussion 5 years later). Net: the project existed/exists as a real, named, sourced proposal, but 'cancelled' (with 2008 as the year) looks unsupported and likely wrong; 'shelved 2006' is actively contradicted by 2006 being a year of forward movement (contract + budget approval). A more defensible characterization on current evidence is 'long-stalled/dormant, revived periodically in talks through at least 2013, never built' -- but I did not find a source stating it is formally dead today either. ROUTE ACCURACY: no source found gives an actual surveyed/mapped route or coordinates -- only endpoint cities (Mellitah, Gabes) and total length. RouteAccuracy=high for a pipeline that was apparently never constructed and for which no route geometry source exists is not supported by anything I found; recommend Update reconsider this field.

resolutions.researcher_notes: (a) Endpoints: CONFIRMED WRONG. The origin akhbarlibya24.net article (2020-05-10, verified) is about a short 4-inch BACKUP gas line built entirely inside the Abu Attifel oil field/Sirte Basin -- from the field's main production station to its own GT11/GT12 power-generation units -- so those units are not solely dependent on the field's NGL plant during its maintenance outages. 'Mellitah' in the headline/row is the operating company (Mellitah Oil & Gas Co., the NOC/Eni JV that operates Abu Attifel), not the geographic Mellitah coastal complex/port ~900-1000 km away. No source supports any pipe running between the two places, and a 4-inch line over that distance would be physically implausible as a transmission trunk, consistent with the brief's expectation. This row's endpoints (StartLocation=Mellitah/Mellitah Port, EndLocation=Bu-Attifel oil field/Sirte Basin) should both be corrected to a single-site location: Abu Attifel field, Sirte Basin, Libya (both start and end within the field). (b) Cancellation: NOT SOURCED. Found no report, in Arabic or English (checked Libya Herald, Libya Observer, Al Wasat, attaqa, eanlibya, NOC.ly, Mellitah OG's own site, Oil Review Africa/Petroleum Africa Abu Attifel coverage 2020-2024), stating this backup line was cancelled, abandoned, or completed. The only source (the 2020-05-10 announcement) describes it as ~60% built and due to finish within weeks -- i.e. near-completion, not a project being scrapped. 'No update since 2020' (the existing researcher note) is silence, not evidence of cancellation, per protocol. GEM's own wiki entry for this PID (read for leads only) in fact currently shows Status='Under construction', contradicting the sheet's 'cancelled' -- suggesting the cancelled status was never substantiated and may be an error/placeholder. Flagging separately per the brief: Status=cancelled also carries NO ShelvedCancelledType, which is itself a data-completeness gap regardless of the status verdict. Scope note for the human reviewer (not my call): if the endpoints are corrected as in (a), this becomes a ~short, likely well-under-1km, 4-inch site utility/backup feeder entirely within one field -- exactly the class of intra-facility service line GGIT's inclusion threshold is generally meant to exclude; worth a explicit in/out-of-scope decision rather than just a location fix.
